observations: Live PLOS article still exposes S1 Code as Code.zip at DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014719.s002.

The article states SPLiT combines online Oja subspace tracking with normalized LMS in manifold coordinates and explicitly notes that similar conditioning gains could come from low-rank projections or pseudoinverse regularization.
Read-only attempts to resolve the S1 Code binary/file-level contents remained blocked in this invocation; no source-exact S8/S11/S12 reproduction was performed.
public_source_audit.scope: Public article inspection plus bounded source-derived synthetic controls; not an exact reproduction of the authors' recurrent network or supporting code.

bounded_audit.status: O(Nk) dormant-subspace-memory stability-plasticity boundary and prequential usefulness gate; non-reproduction

design.generic_tracker: O(Nk) residual-subspace/GROUSE-like update with QR re-orthogonalization; no O(N^2) covariance matrix
design.oja_control: bounded Oja-like online subspace update; not source-exact SPLiT
design.decoder: intrinsic normalized LMS with ambient decoder projection preserved across basis updates
design.memory: decoder-anchored dormant subspace memory; previous task-relevant ambient decoder span weakly anchors the online basis
design.harder_collapse_condition: two distinct task-relevant latent modes become nearly silent over overlapping unknown windows while nuisance directions remain active; target still depends on the silent modes
design.genuine_switch_condition: a fifth structured mode becomes task-relevant while an old task-relevant mode becomes weak, forcing the useful ambient subspace to change
design.prequential_gate: an O(Nk) residual correction model is evaluated before its own update; only sustained prospective loss reduction releases the old memory anchor toward the new subspace

transient_multi_mode_collapse.interpretation: A cheap task-relevant dormant-subspace anchor preserved directions that temporarily vanished from current covariance and sharply reduced reacquisition error after multiple silent-mode episodes.

genuine_task_relevant_subspace_switch.interpretation: The same dormant memory becomes harmful when the task-relevant ambient subspace truly changes; this is a direct stability-plasticity boundary rather than a uniformly beneficial memory mechanism.

prequential_usefulness_gate.interpretation: Prospective residual usefulness largely removed stale-memory harm after a true switch while preserving most collapse benefit, but it still released the anchor spuriously in some temporary-collapse periods and therefore slightly worsened collapse recovery versus the simple anchor. A reliable local task-change detector remains the bottleneck.

oja_like_memory_check.overall_and_early_scope: overall and early-collapse paired intervals included zero; the memory effect was not uniformly beneficial in the Oja-like tracker.
oja_like_memory_check.interpretation: The memory idea is not tracker-invariant. It improved late reacquisition in this bounded Oja-like control but did not provide a clean early or overall advantage, so no Oja-specific or universal memory claim is warranted.

limits: Synthetic linear-latent streams only; not source-exact SPLiT recurrent dynamics or neural data.
The dormant-memory anchor is an engineering control derived from decoder state, not an established biological mechanism.
The prequential gate uses an auxiliary O(Nk) residual predictor and hand-set persistence/thresholds selected for this bounded audit; it is not optimized.
The genuine switch condition changes which ambient latent mode is task-relevant by construction; conclusions apply to this explicit stability-plasticity intervention only.
Source-exact S1 Code, dt/update-order semantics, and published S8/S11/S12 implementation remain unresolved.

candidate_update.positive_scope: In bounded O(Nk) controls, retaining task-relevant dormant subspace directions materially improved recovery when multiple latent modes temporarily disappeared from current covariance. A prospective residual-usefulness gate could release stale memory after a genuine task-relevant subspace switch while retaining most transient-collapse benefit.
candidate_update.negative_boundary: Dormant subspace memory is not uniformly beneficial: without a reliable task-change detector it significantly harms adaptation when the useful ambient subspace truly changes. A simple prequential usefulness gate reduced but did not eliminate the tradeoff, and the same memory did not show a uniform early/overall benefit in the bounded Oja-like tracker. No Oja-specific advantage is established.

exact_next_action: Retry read-only S1 Code recovery. If still blocked, replace the hand-set prequential release threshold with a calibrated local change detector that separates persistent task-relevant residual predictiveness from temporary latent silence without using future labels. Test multiple independent disappearing/reappearing modes, nonlinear manifolds, stochastic task switches, and delayed/sparse error. Compare the same dormant-memory/release mechanism across O(Nk) PAST/GROUSE-like and source-closer Oja trackers with matched update budgets. Keep all conclusions bounded until source-exact S8/S11/S12 code is recovered.
